title: Streaming signal propagation and compact resume token protocol
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: Client disconnects (graceful or abrupt), slow consumers, and transient timeouts cause partial generations to linger in memory and GPU KV caches. Existing heuristics reclaim aggressively and sometimes drop resumability, which causes app-level data loss and poor UX for long-running generations or tool-invoking flows. We need a compatible protocol that: 1) provides precise backpressure signaling between client, SDK, and server runtime, 2) generates a compact, cross-version resume token that is safe to persist and exchange, 3) lets the system compact/tombstone partial generations deterministically, and 4) can be rolled out incrementally with fallbacks to current heuristics.
goals:
- Reduce unrecoverable partial-generation loss by 90% for disconnects that occur within token TTL.
- Keep resume-token size <= 64 bytes when serialized for cookies/DB and SDK storage.
- Add explicit backpressure signals so upstreams can shed load smoothly and keep SLOs.
- Maintain compatibility with HTTP/1.1/2 streaming and current WebSocket and SDK semantics.
constraints_and_assumptions:
- Clients may be offline for up to 15 minutes but should not expect indefinite retention.
- Durable persistence (S3/Blob) available for attachment snapshots; we prefer KV cache + small durable checkpoint.
- Tokens must be revocable (on billing/account change) and verifiable without requiring full server-side session state for basic resume validation.
- We cannot change wire framing for existing SDKs immediately; introduce a compatibility header and a legacy fallback path.
high_level_design:
1) Backpressure signals: define three idempotent wire-level signals: CLIENT_HEARTBEAT (client->server, keep-alive intent), WINDOW_UPDATE (client->server, indicates available token window/credits), and SERVER_DRAIN (server->client, hint that generation will be soft-aborted unless window is extended). SDKs will expose an API: updateWindow(credits), sendHeartbeat(reason). The REST/HTTP2 compatibility layer will map these to HTTP/2 RST/NOOP or custom :path headers for chunk frames for older clients.

2) Compact Resume Token: token = base64url( version||session_prefix_hash[6]||epoch_ms_trunc[6]||seq_uint32||hmac_trunc[8] ). Explanation: version byte (1), 6 bytes of derived prefix hash (sha256 of session id + model+route), 6-byte truncated epoch (ms / 1000 to reduce size), 4-byte sequence, 8-byte truncated HMAC for integrity. Total raw ~25 bytes -> base64 ~34 chars. Token encodes only what is needed to locate the partial generation in persistent index; no PII.

3) Resume handshake: on reconnect, client sends Resume-Token header. Server validates HMAC and prefix match, then performs atomic lock acquisition on generation metadata. If KV prefix present in memory, server streams delta; if only durable checkpoint present, server hydrates prefix into runtime and continues. If validation fails, server returns 410 with the reason.

4) Tombstone/Compaction rules: generations older than TTL (configurable, default 15m) are marked soft-tombstone and eligible for compaction. Compaction follows a two-step: mark -> defer reclaim window (default 2m) -> reclaim. During defer window, resume remains allowed but with degraded success. Compaction also emits a tombstone event to audit-log and customer-facing dashboard.

5) Migration/Compatibility: Introduce opt-in header X-Redwood-ResumeV1. New SDKs will opt-in first; server supports both legacy heuristics and new protocol. We will use feature flag per-tenant to gate behavior and an experiment to measure resume success and cost impact.
storage_and_indexing:
- Lightweight index table: key = prefix_hash(6) + seq, value = pointer to in-memory runtime shard or durable checkpoint location. Index entries TTL aligned with generation TTL.
- Durable checkpoints only contain compacted KV and last N tokens (N configurable, default 4) to limit cold-hydration cost.
- Garbage collector sweeps tombstoned entries asynchronously with batch size throttle tied to autoscaler to avoid thundering-herd on reclaim.
security_considerations:
- Tokens are HMAC-signed with tenant-specific key stored in KMS; revocation handled by key rotation and a short-lived revocation list (RLS).
- Tokens do not include PII or prompt text; only opaque pointers and truncated metadata.
- Audit events emitted for resume success/failure and token minting.
- We will add a small rate limit for resume attempts per session to mitigate abuse.
rollout_plan:
1) Implement server runtime and index (backend-only) behind feature flag. 2) Release SDK update with opt-in header and window API (beta clients). 3) Start a canary for 5% tenants; monitor resume-success-rate, orphaned-generation-count, and cost delta. 4) Expand to 25% -> 100% with staggered GC parameter tightening. 5) Deprecate old aggressive heuristics after 2 successful cycles.
- Rollback: disable feature flag; server cleans partial state and falls back to legacy TTL reclaim.
- Timeline: 6 weeks (2w backend, 2w SDK, 1w canary, 1w expansion).
test_plan:
- Unit tests for token encoding/decoding, HMAC validation, and TTL edge cases.
- Integration tests for resume handshake covering in-memory, durable-hydration, and invalid-token paths.
- Chaos test: kill client mid-stream at random offsets and verify resume token correctness.
- Load test: simulate 10k concurrent resumable generations and measure reclaim throughput and index latency.
- QA: manual end-to-end with SDKs (JS, Python) to verify compatibility fallbacks.
